Scope and Interpretation: Arrows show the progression of research questions; they do not imply that every added module improves every metric. Downside and GARCH models are parallel tests.
Risk budgets are not capital weights. A 0% offensive target returns the strategy to its core portfolio; it does not liquidate the entire portfolio.
Same research period and fixed 0.05% one-way cost. Bubble size represents three annual one-way turnover bands, not portfolio size or statistical confidence.
Calendar-year net returns, not annualized returns. 2015 and 2026 are partial years.

The offensive allocation is the model target carried by each executed order and forward-filled thereafter. It is not a separately drifted offensive sub-account. Qualified breadth is also recorded at execution rather than recalculated daily.

End-of-day holdings are compared under one common EWMA covariance matrix. GMA-CRP was originally optimized with a sample covariance matrix, so it need not show equal risk under this EWMA remeasurement. Neither benchmark targets equal asset-class risk. Cash is retained in the source holdings but contributes no risky-asset variance.

Each snapshot uses the first trade after a preselected date. Risk contributions use the signal-date EWMA covariance matrix. The core solution should closely match its target budget; the final portfolio may depart from that budget after the offensive overlay and trading buffer. Negative contributions may arise from hedging effects.

Regimes use the trailing 63-day GMA-EW return: at least +5% is Rising, at most -5% is Falling, and the remainder is Sideways. This same-day classification is descriptive and ex post; it is not a tradable signal or independent evidence of timing alpha.

The three non-overlapping windows are selected from the deepest GMA-EW drawdown episodes. Each strategy is rebased to 1 at the common window start. Recovery is the first return to 1 after the strategy's trough within that window; unrecovered observations remain missing rather than being recorded as zero days.
